title: Ultrametric Triangle Inequality in p-adic Analysis (OQ-02)
description: Formalizes the ultrametric (strong) triangle inequality for p-adic numbers: ‖q+r‖_p ≤ max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p). Proves the equality case: ‖q‖_p ≠ ‖r‖_p → ‖q+r‖_p = max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p). Applications: isosceles triangle property, ultrametric balls. 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: p-adic norm for the ultrametric inequality

overview.historicalContext: The p-adic numbers ℚ_p carry the p-adic norm ‖·‖_p satisfying the ultrametric inequality ‖q+r‖_p ≤ max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p). This is much stronger than the usual triangle inequality. Consequences: all triangles in ℚ_p are 'isosceles' (two sides equal), and all points in an open ball are centers.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the ultrametric inequality for ℚ_p and its consequences: equality when norms differ, isosceles triangles, and ball properties.
overview.proofStrategy: padicNorm.ultrametric: v_p(q+r) ≥ min(v_p(q), v_p(r)) → ‖q+r‖_p ≤ max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p). Equality case: WLOG v_p(q) > v_p(r), then v_p(q+r) = v_p(r) (the minimum). This gives ‖q+r‖_p = ‖r‖_p = max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p).
keyInsights: **Ultrametric**: ‖q+r‖_p ≤ max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p) follows from v_p(q+r) ≥ min(v_p(q), v_p(r)) and ‖·‖_p = p^{-v_p(·)}.
**Isosceles triangles**: All triangles in ℚ_p are isosceles. If ‖q‖_p ≠ ‖r‖_p, then ‖q+r‖_p = max(‖q‖_p, ‖r‖_p), so two sides equal the third.
**Ultra-balls**: Every point in an open ball B(x,r) is its center. B(x,r) = B(y,r) for any y ∈ B(x,r).

conclusion.summary: p-adic ultrametric theory: 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The ultrametric inequality is the foundation of p-adic analysis and has deep number-theoretic implications. The isosceles triangle property distinguishes p-adic geometry from Euclidean geometry.
openQuestions: Can the p-adic Mahler measure and its properties be formalized?
Can the Weierstrass preparation theorem for ℤ_p be proved?
Can Hensel's lemma be formally derived from the ultrametric property?
